overall: The AG found five councilors violated the OML by sending a zoning opinion letter to the rest of the council, reaching a quorum outside a posted meeting; the other allegations (drafting, notice specificity, lack of discussion) were not violations. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Five councilors sent a letter giving their opinions on proposed zoning amendments to the remaining councilors outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: when the five Councilors sent the letter containing their opinions on proposed zoning ordinances to the remaining Councilors outside of a posted meeting, thus reaching a quorum, they violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The five councilors allegedly coordinated and drafted the zoning letter outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: as these five Councilors did not constitute a quorum of the Council.

allegations.summary: Fourteen of the 25 agenda items in the June 5 notice allegedly lacked enough detail about funds, purpose, enterprise accounts, or the issue involved.
allegations.key_passage: we are satisfied that the meeting notice satisfied the Open Meeting Law’s specificity requirement.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly voted on agenda items at the June 5 meeting with little or no discussion beforehand.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by voting on matters without first engaging in discussion.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
